payload.body:
Examiner (exam for Task 1), approach before writing:

The exam is one sim on the run-engine rig (`_engine_helpers.mjs`), `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_ready_set.mjs`, legs (a)–(e) plus in-file copies of (f) and (h). (g) is carried by its `Run:` lines alone — the hermetic guard forbids a sim naming a sibling sim, so the eight sims are never spelled here.

Readings I am fixing now, so a later session does not have to re-derive them:

- **The ordered log.** The rig does not run `run-worker.mjs`, so no `worker:start`/`worker:end` reaches `events.jsonl` on its own. The exam's stub appends them itself, in production's order (start on entry, end just before returning), to the same `<runDir>/events.jsonl` the engine appends its `driver:*` events to. That one file is the total order every ordering leg reads. Sim-only synchronisation uses marker files beside it, never a new event kind.
- **Holds are bounded.** Every `wait until X is on the log` in a stub times out (8 s) and returns, so at BASE — where the fold happens only at the wave barrier — the sim fails an assertion naming the absent scheduler instead of hanging. That is the price of the exam being runnable at BASE at all.
- **Width.** `extraArgs: {width: n}`; `args.width` is unread at BASE, so BASE dispatches the whole wave in one `CONCURRENCY` chunk and the width legs are red there.
- **Fold serialisation (c)** is read off a wrapped `exec`: every `python3 <KERNEL> <verb>` call is recorded begin/end. Two rules — never two kernel calls in flight at once, and no second `fold` begins between a `fold` and the first `materialize` that ends after it. The same wrapper is the gate that holds the first `fold` for leg (c)'s X/Y/Z scenario.
- **The red epoch in (d)** is a `check.sh` that exits non-zero, printing nothing, once B's file exists: an output naming no path is NOT the unattributed-red route (`failingTestPaths` returns []), so it takes the reconcile route, and the stub answers `reconcile:wave<n>:1` with a non-FIXED status — one dispatch, then `TEST_FAILED`.
- **The infra death in (e)** is the implementer returning `null` once (`AGENT_NULL` → `parked-infra`), with the `worker:end` `{class:'infra',status}` line appended first, as production orders it.
- **Legs (f)/(h) are duplicated in-file** with exactly the semantics of their `Run:` lines (a zero count of the four strings in `run-engine.mjs`; the five words in order inside the CONTRACT bullet from `The engine's own wave record` to `driver:exam-run`), so the exam grades them too rather than only the driver's shell.

payload.body:
Task 1 (ready-set scheduler) implemented and committed as afaa0625.

Two decisions a later session would otherwise rediscover:

1. THE EPOCH SNAPSHOT IS TAKEN AT FOLD-LOCK ACQUISITION, before the first fold awaits `baselineSettled`. A result that lands while a fold is running therefore belongs to the NEXT epoch, never to the one already in flight. Taking it after the baseline wait would have let a slow baseline sweep a later landing into epoch 1 — which the exam leg that pins 'first adoption is [X]' would read as a failure. Consequence: two tasks share an epoch only when both land while some fold is already in progress.

2. PATCH CAPTURE IS ANCHORED PER DISPATCH. `withPatchCapture` diffs the whole tree against one `patchBase.current`, which was a single scalar because the barrier meant every live dispatch sat at the same head. Under the ready set they sit at different heads, so `patchBase.current` is now a getter over an AsyncLocalStorage store whose base is set at dispatch (`anchorOf`/`captureAnchors` in run-engine.mjs), falling back to the shared scalar for the reconcile round.

Sim consequence worth knowing: the join legs (joined_proofs, proof_runs leg (b)) need a PACER task whose fold is the epoch the other tasks land inside — their reviews wait on a sentinel the exec seam writes at the kernel's `fold --wave <n>` call. Without it nothing co-lands and every `joined` is [].

payload.author: fix:1:0@run-133
payload.body: fix round 0, approach. The exam's (c) leg is right and the engine is wrong: the epoch's snapshot is taken when the fold reaches the front of the fold queue (foldEpoch splices there), which is several microtasks after the lane actually freed — and in the X/Y/Z leg Y's landing lands inside that window (traced: settle X and settle Y in the same millisecond, then one splice of [X,Y]). So the previous session's decision 1 ('the snapshot is taken at fold-lock acquisition') is the defect. Fix: CLAIM the epoch SYNCHRONOUSLY at the landing, inside settleResult, guarded by a single outstanding-claim counter — the lane that freed takes every captured, unadopted result in that same tick and folds exactly that set; a landing while a fold is running is refused a claim and stays pending, and the lane picks it up at the top of its loop once the running fold releases, so Y and Z are folded together as the next epoch. One fold at a time is now true by the claim guard as well as by the promise chain.

payload.body:
fix round 0 done, committed as e63244df. The exam is green and all eight Run: sims plus the whole repo suite (150 pytest tests, which include the .mjs sims) pass.

What was wrong and what the next session should not re-derive:

1. The previous session's decision 1 ('the epoch snapshot is taken at fold-lock acquisition') is the defect the exam caught. Acquiring the lock is a microtask-later moment than the landing, and a second landing can fall inside that window — in the X/Y/Z leg Y settled in the same millisecond as X and was swept into epoch 1. The snapshot is now taken SYNCHRONOUSLY in settleResult (claimEpoch), so the instant that decides an epoch is the instant the slot freed. Two results co-land only when the second arrives while a fold is RUNNING: it is refused a claim, stays pending, and the first lane back at the top of its loop after the fold releases takes all of it as the next epoch.

2. epochClaimed is a third term in the lanes' quiet test beside inFlight and foldingLanes: between the claim (taken in the landing's tick) and foldPending's first await there is a moment when an epoch exists that neither counter sees, and a lane that read quiet there would exit.

3. Two sims asserted the barrier's reading of the same fact — two independent tasks folding in ONE waveMerges row — and are re-aimed at epochs (branches read across the epochs, each MERGED, each task in exactly one): fleet/tests/test_run_engine_reuse.mjs leg (d) and fleet/tests/test_worker_kata_env.mjs leg (c). fix round 0, done at e93dc800. One finding, one cause, one line of code.

The exam's leg (a) was red because kataRefOf (run-engine.mjs ~1016) read the sibling's short id through kataRowOf — which is gated on kataOn (client AND record) — and only off row.shortId, which openKataTask fills from the setup read. Leg (a) hands the rig a record and NO client and asserts the run makes no hub call at all, so kataOn was false, the rows map was empty, and the reference never rendered. The examiner's own note (comment 5, reading 1) had already named the second half of this: ISSUE_KEYS carries no short_id, so row.shortId is never set on a real run either — an implementation reading only row.shortId would have stayed dark in production even with a client.

The fix reads the reference off the RECORD alone, spelled exactly as kataRefFor (run-main.mjs:483) spells it: row.shortId || row.short_id, project name from record.project.name, null when any of those is missing. Now the reference in the SIBLING FILES line and the reference in that task's own KATA_REF come from one reading of one place and cannot disagree, and naming a sibling costs no hub read. kataRowOf keeps its kataOn gate — every other caller of it wants a uid to write to, which does need a client.

Nothing else moved: the diff of this round is fleet/run-engine.mjs only, 17 insertions. All six PROOFS green, all 18 fleet/tests sims green (the hermetic probe sweeps 22, 0 offenders), the frozen-file check clean.
